thesis_summary.thesis: Willis Towers Watson (WTW) is a global advisory, broking, and solutions company focused on people, risk, and capital. **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$9.7 billion** (-2% reported, **+5% organic**), split between **Health, Wealth & Career (HWC)** at **$5.3 billion** (~55% of segment revenue) and **Risk & Broking (R&B)** at **$4.3 billion** (~45%). **[Fact]** The company earns commissions on insurance placements (tied to carrier premium levels), fee-based consulting on employee benefits and executive compensation, and outsourced benefits administration. **[Fact]** FY2025 operating cash flow was **$1.8 billion**; capital expenditures and capitalized software were **$229 million**; share repurchases **$1.65 billion**; dividends **$358 million**. **[Fact]** Q1 2026 revenue was **$2.4 billion** (+8.5% versus $2.2 billion prior year) with diluted EPS **$3.10** (+33%).
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: There is **no dated mispricing catalyst** (HK predictive attribute: **none**). **[Inference]** The market may anchor on the **2024 goodwill impairment** ($1.0 billion, TRANZACT-related) and reported net income of **$98 million**, underweighting the normalized **$1.6 billion** FY2025 net income and **+5% organic** revenue trajectory. **[Fact]** Management simplified the portfolio: sold TRANZACT (Dec 2024), received **$750 million** Willis Re earnout (2025), and acquired tech-broker **Newfront** (Dec 2025). **[Inference]** Generalists treating WTW as a pure P&C cycle play may miss the fee-durable HWC consulting mix and international health growth (double-digit organic in FY2025). The edge is **quality franchise at ~18 times owner cash**, not a timed yield-curve setup.

Goodwill **$10+ billion** on balance sheet warrants monitoring; 2024 impairment was TRANZACT-related, not core HWC/R&B.
No third-party sources indexed; stance is Marvin floor only.
